A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multi-task evidence-aggregation framework, with matching core experiments and theoretical results. The main text, figures, table and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original RNN/LSTM experiments, OOD decoding results, attractor analyses and task variants in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds GPT-2 comparisons, decoder-angle measurements, dynamical analyses and noise-robustness results.

M1.justification: V2 changes the main fixed-reaction-time classifier from MSE/tanh with ±1 targets to cross-entropy/sigmoid with 0/1 targets. It also introduces a continuous-input GPT-2 implementation without tokenization or positional encodings (Section 4; Appendix A.5). The earlier MSE/tanh formulation remains in the free-reaction-time comparison.

E1.justification: The synthetic evidence-aggregation domain and linear, nonlinear and free-reaction-time task families remain. V2 adds anisotropic Gaussian, temporally correlated AR(1) and Gumbel noise scenarios (Appendix A.8), while removing v1's scenario with classification boundaries restricted to two quadrants.

E2.justification: GPT-2 joins the architecture comparison containing leaky RNNs, non-leaky RNNs and LSTMs (v1 Figure 1g; v2 Figure 3b), and is compared against RNNs across input dimensionalities in Figure 5b. This substantially expands the comparative architecture evidence. The context-dependent RNN comparison is retained in Appendix A.7.

E3.justification: V2 extends evaluation beyond decoding r2 and trajectory visualization to pairwise decoder angles and Jacobian eigenspectra (Appendices A.3 and A.6). The new GPT experiments use 20,000 training batches, versus the retained 100,000-batch RNN setting. The existing quadrant-based cross-validation protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct orthogonality measurements, local dynamical-stability analysis, GPT activation analysis and tests of alternative noise assumptions. It removes the standalone multiplicative-task failure analysis and the restricted-boundary analysis from v1. Interleaved learning, correlated inputs and free-reaction-time analyses are retained, largely through relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions describe five trained networks, five decoder fits per held-out quadrant, and reporting of the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles. V2 applies the same practice to decoder-angle measurements. No increased repetition count or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds GPT performance and geometry results, stability spectra, and noise-robustness medians: r2 = 0.96 for anisotropic noise and 0.95 for AR(1) and Gumbel noise (Appendix A.8). Removed results include multiplicative-only r2 = 0.71 and restricted-boundary median r2 = 0.80, with lower quartile 0.62. The changed main training objective prevents interpreting revised plots as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds explicit representation definitions, sigmoid Corollary B.8, orthogonality Corollary B.9, and general-noise extensions including anisotropic Gaussian Lemma B.10. The main theorem distinguishes decodability at Ntask >= D from orthogonality at Ntask >> D. These materially extend v1's Gaussian/tanh development, although the new inverse-CDF reconstruction in Appendix B.4 has an internal sign inconsistency.

C1.justification: V1 largely equates linear decodability with disentanglement when tasks span the latent space. V2 separates this claim from orthogonal disentanglement, adding a stronger task-number condition for the latter. Its abstract and contributions also introduce transformer disentanglement at Ntask >= D as a principal finding.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting transformer generalization to orthogonality and interpreting noise-CDF/activation mismatch as geometric distortion. It explicitly places multiplicative boundaries outside the theorem's coverage, while removing v1's explanations of multiplicative-only failure and inadequate boundary coverage. The factorization assumption and lack of standard ML benchmarks remain acknowledged limitations.

D1.justification: V2 supplies GPT-specific architecture and training details, decoder-angle and Jacobian-analysis procedures, and an explicit one-layer RNN/LSTM setting in Table S1. Most existing RNN hyperparameters remain unchanged. V1's NeuroGym implementation statement and approximate ten-minute laptop-CPU training-time disclosure are removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against Roeder et al.'s linear-identifiability work, adopts definitions from Ostojic and Fusi, and adds references supporting noise and manifold arguments. Some broad foundation-model citations are removed. The central relationship to Johnston and Fusi's multi-task representation work remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. Problem formulation and methods become separate sections, the experiment narrative is reorganized around generalization and representational geometry, and nonlinear/free-reaction-time material moves into Appendix A. The discussion is extensively reorganized and the separate conclusion disappears.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 1 is redistributed across v2 Figures 1–3, the free-reaction-time figure moves to Figure S4, and the former supplementary activation figure becomes an expanded RNN/GPT comparison in Figure 4. New angle, spectral and CDF-approximation displays are added; multiplicative-only and restricted-boundary panels are removed.

improvement.justification: Direct angle measurements and stability analyses address gaps in v1's empirical support, while GPT and noise experiments broaden the evidence. However, v2 removes informative failure analyses and introduces inconsistencies in its expanded theory: Equation 25 contains an extra C-transpose factor, and Appendix B.4's inverse-CDF step has the opposite sign implied by its preceding equation. These empirical gains and losses in completeness and theoretical reliability leave the net quality change unclear.
